name: Isolated Focal Cortical Dysplasia Type Ia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) Classification of Focal Cortical Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of abnormal cortical lamination with dysmorphic neurons without balloon cells on histopathological examination
Focal onset seizures often refractory to medical treatment
MRI evidence of focal cortical thickening or blurring of the gray-white matter junction in the affected region
Electroencephalogram (EEG) showing focal epileptiform discharges correlating with clinical seizure focus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of abnormal cortical lamination with dysmorphic neurons plus clinical focal seizures and supportive MRI findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires histopathology from surgical specimen; MRI and EEG findings support clinical suspicion.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal onset seizures with impaired awareness

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment related to seizure burden
searchTerms: memory and learning issues related to seizures
seizure activity between episodes on EEG

occasional.symptomName: Mood disturbances including anxiety and depression
searchTerms: mood changes including sadness and worry
temporary weakness on one side after seizure

rare.symptomName: Visual field deficits related to lesion location
searchTerms: blind spots related to brain lesion

imaging: MRI showing focal cortical thickening, blurring of gray-white matter junction, and transmantle sign in some cases
other: Histopathology demonstrating abnormal cortical lamination with dysmorphic neurons without balloon cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of balloon cells on histopathology
Multisystem involvement with skin lesions, renal angiomyolipomas

redFlags: New onset focal seizures refractory to multiple antiepileptic drugs
references: Blumcke I, et al. The clinicopathologic spectrum of focal cortical dysplasias: a consensus classification proposed by an ad hoc Task Force of the ILAE Diagnostic Methods Commission. Epilepsia. 2011 Jun;52(1):158-74.
Wong M. Mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathways in neurological diseases. Biochem Soc Trans. 2013 Apr;41(4):1113-7.
